summary: Four-legged steel lookout tower near Kinston, 85 ft in 1975 and then North Carolina Forest Service property; no source found describes its condition today.

events.note: National Geodetic Survey described the tower for survey mark EY2575 (designated Kellys Pond Lot)

evidence.quote: KELLYS POND LOOKOUT TOWER, IS A FOUR LEGGED, SELF SUPPORTED STEEL

evidence.supports: Tower about 2.5 miles southeast of Kinston
evidence.quote: THE TOWER IS LOCATED ABOUT 2-1/2 MILES SOUTHEAST OF KINSTON,

evidence.supports: Described by National Geodetic Survey in 1975
Height 85 feet in 1975 description (converted to 25.9 m)
evidence.quote: WITH THE OVER HEIGHT OF 85 FEET

evidence.supports: Property of the North Carolina Forest Service

evidence.supports: Survey mark at top center of the roof

Tower listed in NCDOT Kinston Bypass historical features as Kelly’s Pond Fire Lookout Tower
NCDOT effect decision for the tower: no adverse effect
List entry: Kellys Pond, Lenoir county, EY2575

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NGS and the tnlandforms list write Kellys Pond; the NCDOT list writes Kelly’s Pond Fire Lookout Tower. The name and place match, so this is a spelling difference only.

sources.title: NGS Data Sheet for survey mark EY2575, Kellys Pond Lot

notes_for_editor: Brief status and access are unknown and stay that way. The NGS datasheet is the main source. Its last dated entry is a 2008 recovery of the mark, and no later source was found. The 85 ft height and the North Carolina Forest Service ownership are 1975 figures, so they are not in facts.agency and are not presented as current. The NCDOT PDF is undated in our cache. The brief coordinates are about 44 m from the NGS mark, so no correction is proposed. A WebSearch hit on Kellys Pond (the NCpedia lake entry) is a different place and was not used.
